subject: Multi-year prepay proposal — Novum Analytics (ramp & executive approval)
messages:
From: Dan Hayes <dan.hayes@novumanalytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@novumanalytics.com>, procurement@novumanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Multi-year pricing — initial ask (Novum RFP)

Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Novum is preparing an RFP for platform inference for our analytics products. We like Redwood's latency profile and the deployment flexibility. Our procurement team needs pricing for a 3-year prepay with an atypical ramp — heavy commitment year 1 (40% of total committed spend), 30% year 2, 30% year 3.

Given the volume, we're looking for a more aggressive blended discount in year 1 (we've seen asks in the 40-55% range from other vendors). Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a 3-year prepay with that ramp and what a term discount would look like? Also need net-60 invoicing and our standard PO process. Attached is our RFP and volume estimates.

Goal: get a commercial term sheet by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Dan Hayes
Head of Infrastructure Purchasing
Novum Analytics

Attachment: Novum_RFP_20260201.pdf
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Dan Hayes <dan.hayes@novumanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing — initial ask (Novum RFP)

Dan —

Appreciate the RFP and the clarity on the ramp. Short answer: we can support multi-year prepays with custom ramp schedules, but the discount profile you propose (40-55% year 1) is beyond standard prepay tiers we publish. I've attached a preliminary term table showing a few options: 24-month and 36-month prepay curves, and one custom ramp that approximates your numbers.

What I'll do next:
- Loop in our sales leadership and finance for an exec approval if we need to go beyond published tiers.
- Share an internal counter with constraints (payment terms, milestone-triggered discounts, or escrow).
- If you can, share the PO process timeline and who signs — that will speed approvals.

I'll try to get an internal decision today and follow up with either a conditional term sheet or a request for exec sign-off.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_multipay_term_table.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Multi-year pricing — Novum request (need exec approval)

Dylan —

Forwarding this. Novum is asking for an aggressive early-year discount and wants net-60. This is a large ARR opportunity (attached volumes = ~ $4.2M/year list if they fully utilize). If we accept a 50%+ year 1 discount with standard prepay accounting, our NPV and cash profile change materially.

Asking Vivek and Neha: can we approve a custom ramp with the customer-proposed percentages if we impose milestone-based payment (year 1 release tied to deployment milestones) and require PO up front? Options to consider:
- Option A: 36-month prepay, 35% year1 discount, 20% year2, 15% year3, with escrow holdback for first 6 months.
- Option B: Approve 45% year1 discount but require 60% payment upfront and remaining 40% in two equal installments on day 365 and day 730.
- Option C: Decline heavy year1 discount; offer stepped discount (25%/20%/15%) + usage overage PRICING.

This needs a VP-level sign-off to deviate from published tiers. Please advise quickly — customer wants terms by Friday.

Marissa
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Multi-year pricing — Novum request (need exec approval)

Thanks for the context. Novum is strategically interesting (analytics OEM + large north american footprint). I'm willing to approve a one-time exception on the discount curve provided Finance signs off on the cash schedule and Legal signs an escrow/milestone clause.

High-level direction:
- Approve Option B as a starting point (higher upfront payment, larger year1 discount) subject to Neha confirming acceptable cash flow and minimal clawback language.
- Require procurement to agree to net-60 only after we receive the first installment (or a warranty escrow).
- Ask Revenue Ops (Laura) to model billing recognition impacts.

Marissa/Dylan: please prepare an internal redlineable term sheet and include explicit trigger milestones (prod-ready, 30-day prod acceptance, usage threshold). Once Neha signs off, I'll prepare an executive approval note.

Vivek
VP Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 16:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Multi-year pricing — Novum request (need exec approval)

Team —

I ran the numbers on the attached finance model. Key notes:
- At a 45-50% year1 discount with full list recognition, the effective NPV at our cost of capital is marginal unless we collect >= 60% of total upfront.
- Net-60 is fine operationally but we need cash certainty for any deeper tier. My recommendation: accept Option B but require 60% prepayment (escrow/lockbox) and the remainder split into two 12-month invoices. If Novum insists on net-60 for the first installment, require a signed irrevocable PO and parent company guaranty.
- Also recommend a clawback clause for early termination within 18 months pro-rated recapture.

Attachments: finance_model_NV-2026-0047.xlsx

If the customer agrees to 60% upfront, I can sign off and authorize legal to finalize.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Finance, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Dan Hayes <dan.hayes@novumanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 09:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing — Novum request (term sheet & DocuSign)

Dan —

Thanks for your patience. Per internal approvals, we can move forward on a conditional executive-approved prepay structure:
- 36-month total term; 45% discount applied to year1 committed spend, year2 and year3 stepped lower (detailed in attached term sheet).
- Payment schedule: 60% due at signing (escrow/lockbox), 20% due at 12 months, 20% due at 24 months.
- Net-60 invoicing for follow-ups only after first installment is received.
- Clawback: pro-rated recapture for termination within 18 months.

I've attached the redlined term table and the draft term sheet. Please review. If this aligns, I can send a DocuSign envelope for an initial signature and provide our standard PO/invoice workflow.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/REDACTED_DOCUSIGN_LINK
Attachment: redwood_multipay_term_table.xlsx

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Dan Hayes <dan.hayes@novumanalytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@novumanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@novumanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year pricing — Novum request (term sheet & DocuSign)

Dylan —

Thanks — this is close to what we need. Procurement is willing to accept the 60% upfront if Redwood will:
1) Provide a milestone schedule tied to deployment (we'll sign off on acceptance tests).
2) Allow our AP team net-60 on the remaining invoices and provide an invoice/PO that matches our accounting fields (we attach our PO template).

We're ready to review the DocuSign term sheet. Alex in procurement will coordinate with our legal on clawback wording. If legal signs off, we can move to signature next week.

Dan Hayes
Head of Infrastructure Purchasing
Novum Analytics

Attachment: Novum_PO_template.docx
